summary: Multiplexed proxy token flip omits closing paragraph on SSE multipart stream
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a class of SSE streaming responses where the final paragraph (closing paragraph) is never emitted. The stream begins normally and intermediate chunks arrive; however, after a short mid-stream proxy reconnect or HTTP/2 stream multiplexing event, the runtime sends a truncated terminal event and the final closing paragraph is missing. The payload appears valid up to the last emitted chunk; the terminal JSON/choice metadata arrives but the last textual paragraph is absent.

Impact:
- Customer chat sessions are missing the final paragraph in ~3-4% of long multi-paragraph responses for a specific traffic pattern.
- Affects user-visible content quality; customers reported degraded UX and downstream truncation handling.

Environment:
- Customer: NovaSearch Inc. (dedicated cluster)
- Region: us-east (edge -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime)
- Client pattern: HTTP/2 multiplexed connections behind a corporate layer-7 proxy that performs quick connection rebinds for stickiness.
- Model: redwood-13b-compat (pinned for dedicated environment)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided simplified):
1) Start a long prompt that produces 3+ paragraphs (approx 400-800 tokens).
2) Keep client connection open; exercise simultaneous parallel streams on same TCP connection.
3) Trigger a controlled proxy rebind (customer simulates with a quick stickiness change on their proxy).
4) Observe streaming SSE session: final closing paragraph missing ~30% of the time under their proxy conditions.

Expected behavior:
- Stream emits all tokens and final paragraph, plus terminal metadata event, consistently even when upstream proxy rebinds occur.

Observed behavior:
- Middle and penultimate chunks arrive intact. After a short proxy-side session flip, the server-side terminal metadata is emitted but the final paragraph content is absent. In some reproductions the client receives a terminal marker without the trailing whitespace/punctuation.

Attached logs (redacted):
- Correlated request IDs where issue observed: req-20260310-9a7b, req-20260310-9a9f, req-20260310-a0b1
- Edge proxy logs show quick 302->reset sequence and new session token during the stream window.
- Runtime trace shows normal tokenization and choice assembly up to final chunk, then a brief "session token mismatch" event 90-120ms before terminal event.

Notes:
- Customer confirms disabling multiplexing on the client side eliminates the symptom for them (workaround).
- Issue reproduces only when the traffic is routed through their enterprise proxy with the rebind behavior; not observed in our public test harness with identical prompts.

Hypothesis: the edge accepts the terminal event but upstream chunk is lost during connection tearover.

2026-03-11 16:10 - Rafael Ortiz (SRE): Validated edge logs: when proxy rebind occurs, we see quick connection close + new connection accepted; some in-transit write acknowledgements are not synchronized with multiplexed stream mapping, leading to dropped last-chunk data on the edge side.

2026-03-12 10:55 - Support (Maya Chen): Shared customer-impact mitigation steps and asked customer to test a targeted client-side retry that delays finalization by 200ms; customer agreed to test and will report results by EOD.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge/proxy rebind causes RST_STREAM semantics overlapping with final chunk write; edge marks stream complete and discards trailing chunk body.
Hypothesis 2: Multiplexed HTTP/2 stream mapping at our edge lacks ordering guarantees during in-flight session token swap; writes can be acknowledged out-of-band and lost.
Observed: In all failing traces terminal metadata arrives but content length is shorter than expected by 60-120 bytes (consistent with missing final paragraph).
PCAP from customer shows single TCP connection where two logical H2 streams flip affinity; server-side logs show last-chunk queued at t0, RST_STREAM at t0+30ms, terminal emitted at t0+70ms.

Reproducibility: Customer environment strong (30% under their proxy conditions), internal repro without their proxy is rare.
Action: requested deeper edge logs for wire-level ordering and increased tracing on h2 stream lifecycle.
resolution:
Workaround: Customer can disable HTTP/2 multiplexing or add a ~200-300ms client-side delay before finalization to allow pending writes to flush; both mitigate the issue.
Root cause: race between edge connection rebind (proxy-side token flip) and our edge's stream finalization path that allowed terminal metadata to be forwarded before the last text chunk write was durably flushed to the connection mapping.
Permanent fix plan: edge team will implement an idempotent finalization handshake so that the serving runtime waits for a confirmed flush/ack from the edge mapping before emitting the terminal event to the customer. Runtime patch (PR #2431) adds aggressive flush and retry on final chunk and an additional sequence check on the edge.
Rollout notes: will deploy a canary to edge-nodes in us-east first; target deploy window 2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC. Customer impact expected to be resolved post-canary.
Follow-ups: add e2e test that simulates proxy rebinds during chunk flush; update streaming runbook with guidance for client multiplexing and recommended backoff.
notes: Customer prefers server-side fix; support to coordinate announcement and post-deploy verification.
Consider adding explicit header to indicate "final-chunk-flush" semantics for customers behind aggressive proxies as short-term opt-in flag.
Related to INT-1198 where an internal ticket captured an edge-connection-affinity race in a different context.
